chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who incurred major ritual impurity (janabah) during travel, and he had with him only a little water, and he feared that if he were to perform ghusl he would become thirsty. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he fears thirst, let him not spill a single drop from it, and let him perform tayammum with the soil, for the soil is more beloved to me.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a traveler has very little water and fears thirst if they use it for ritual purification?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of prioritizing survival (drinking) over ritual purity (ghusl) when resources are scarce, a key concept in Shia fiqh regarding 'necessity permits the prohibited.' Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explicitly prefers tayammum in this scenario, highlighting that the spiritual merit of the soil is elevated when it serves the higher objective of preserving life, rather than merely substituting for water. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in balancing ritual obligations with practical necessities during travel.
